text:
marco: Heads up — working doc idea for mixed-capacity guardrails. want to finalize min on-demand reserve + burst behavior before monday.
priya: +1. do we have new data on spot interruption rates in us-west-2? last week looked noisy.
alex: us-west-2 P-cores had ~8% interruptions over the 7d window, but 96th percentile uptime per GPU was still ~22h. distribution matters for long seq workloads.
marco: thinking: keep a hard min-reserve (% of total vGPU slots) per region + per-tenant soft ceiling for burst credits. example: min_reserve = 12% for critical tenants, 6% for others.
jamie: can we express it as credits? so burst uses credit bucket, replenishes at steady rate, drains on spot usage. easier to reason about than raw slot counts.
sofia: agree on credits. need to couple with request class: low-latency interactive requests should never be served from spot unless credits > X and model tolerant flag set.
priya: propose policy snippet:
```
policy:
  min_on_demand: 0.12
  burst_pool_ratio: 3
  credit_replenish_rate_per_min: 0.05
  max_credit: 10
  interactive_spot_threshold: 2.0
```
alex: nit: `burst_pool_ratio` ambiguous. does it mean 3x on-demand capacity or 3x spot slots? clarify in doc.
marco: meant 3x transient headroom relative to the min_on_demand; will reword to `burst_headroom_multiplier`.
jamie: interruption handling: immediate plan should 1) gracefully drain to KV cache serialization, 2) re-route to on-demand fallback, 3) decrement tenant credit at time of preempt. need SLO for fallback < 250ms added latency.
sofia: +1 on SLO. also add automatic roll-forward: if fallback model is a smaller quantized variant, tag outputs with `served_via=fallback` and emit metric `fallback_rate` per route.
priya: metrics to track: `spot_interruption_rate`, `burst_credit_balance`, `fallback_latency_p50/p95`, `eviction_retries`, `tenant_cost_savings_pct`.
opsbot: INFO 2026-03-18T14:12:09Z capacity-controller: scheduled 48 spot->on-demand migrations in us-west-2 due to spot price spike.
alex: opsbot log means we should simulate sudden reclaim: two quick tests — (A) cold-switch where we launch on-demand replacements, (B) warm-cache where we keep prefix KV in a hot cache and retry.
marco: test plan: run synthetic workload with long-seq (~2048 tokens) and mix of interactive + batch. ramp spot reclaim events at 10%, 30%, 60% of pool and measure user p99 latency and token loss.
jamie: for routing, prefer model-level compatibility: route to same architecture family, prefer quantized fallback only if quality delta < threshold. add `quality_regression_alert` per rollout.
sofia: network constraints: some regions have limited spare NIC throughput — bursting too aggressively causes cross-pod TCP saturation. add a per-node egress budgeting to burst controller.
priya: cost tradeoff thought: raising min_on_demand reduces interruptions but increases baseline cost. compute pareto curve offline then pick defaults that keep marginal cost < 8% for +50% uptime.
marco: outcome proposals:
- default min_on_demand: 8% region-wide
- critical tenants default: 14% (config override)
- burst via credit buckets with multiplier 2.5
- interactive requests opt-out of spot unless tenant sets `allow_spot_interactive: true`
- expose `fallback_rate` and `credit_balance` in console + alerts at >5% fallback rate sustained for 10m
please react with :thumbsup: if you agree, or drop concerns.
alex: :thumbsup:
priya: few comments in doc, but overall :thumbsup:
sofia: one more ask — add preemptive kube-sigterm + 10s delay to flush KV. otherwise we lose 1-2 tokens for streaming sessions.
marco: added. i'll push a PR to infra/playbooks and schedule a tabletop on friday to run the sim. thanks everyone :wave:
